results.explanation: At the declared notes POST entry, the handler binds the authenticated request user to currentUser and resolves the target document, including its owner. The global PaperlessNotePermissions check is a separate entry permission check: for POST it requires add_note, view_document, and change_document globally. The supplied premise grants those global permissions, so that check does not by itself deny the request. The handler then performs a separate owner-aware object view check; under the premise that the caller has object view access, this also passes. In the POST branch, the decisive control is a separate owner-aware change_document check. The owner-aware helper allows the owner or a Guardian object-permission grant; because the supplied premise says the document is owned by another user and the caller has no object change_document grant, this check is false and the handler returns HTTP 403 before Note.objects.create. Therefore the source-visible behavior at the declared-entry boundary is deny, and the protected note-creation effect is not reached. This assessment covers the supplied entry, identity/resource binding, global permission check, object view check, object change check, and Note.objects.create effect only; source discovery is not-tested and no repository-wide or deployment conclusion is made.

entry.statement: The declared entry is the detail action with POST enabled and PaperlessNotePermissions applied, entering the notes handler.

binding.statement: The handler binds the request identity as currentUser before resolving and authorizing the document.
The handler resolves the target Document by pk and loads its owner information.

control.statement: For POST, PaperlessNotePermissions requires the three global permissions add_note, view_document, and change_document, and checks them with has_perms.
The POST branch separately checks owner-aware change_document permission and returns forbidden when that check fails.
Before method dispatch, the handler separately applies an owner-aware view_document check and returns forbidden if it fails.

effect.statement: Note.objects.create is the protected note-creation effect, executed only after the object change check passes.

condition.statement: The owner-aware helper permits an object when it is unowned, owned by the user, or the object-permission checker grants the requested permission.

citations.quote:
def has_perms_owner_aware(user, perms, obj):
    """
    Legacy slow path (guardian-backed) single-object permission check.

    The queryset-filtering side of this migrated onto
    ``PermittedObjectsFilter``/``permitted_object_ids()``, but this
    single-object check still has many production callers. Several callers
    remain across ``documents/``, ``paperless_mail/``, and ``paperless_ai/``
    -- grep for this function name before removing it.
    """
    checker = ObjectPermissionChecker(user)
    return obj.owner is None or obj.owner == user or checker.has_perm(perms, obj)
